newsitem.title: UK: BCCI creditors to get first payment this wk - report.
newsitem.headline: BCCI creditors to get first payment this wk - report.

text.p: Creditors of the collapsed Bank of Credit and Commerce International (BCCI) will receive their first payments this week, the Times newspaper reported on Monday.
The report quoted the group's British liquidators, Deloitte and Touche, as saying they hoped to make a second payment within the next 12 months.
BCCI collapsed in 1991 with debts of around $10 billion.
The Times said the first payment would be in the order of 24-1/2 percent of the amount owed to creditors, with a second payment possibly around 10 percent.

The bulk of the payment will be made from $1.55 billion paid to the bank's liquidators by the government of Abu Dhabi, BCCI's main shareholder. The Times said Abu Dhabi was due to pay a further $150 million in April 1998 and $100 million shortly afterwards. An additional $500 million has been recovered by receivers.
Payments to creditors have been delayed by a series of challenges, mainly in Luxembourg where BCCI was founded.
